summary: Analyzed the four pinned requests (ver_0mwgrru4w0g357e77d2). Requests syn-req-001, syn-req-003 and syn-req-004 share one need: a policy-configured dataset freshness check that reports "unknown" for unmeasured datasets and is reusable across teams. syn-req-002 asks for schema-contract drift checks, a different signal, so it is listed as unrelated to this capability and flagged as a possible sibling. Each consolidated request keeps its own distinct need. Nothing was written to disk; the report is returned in artifacts.

criteria_claims.note: Shared capability named in shared_capability. Consolidated ids 001, 003, 004 each have a distinct_needs entry in their own stakeholder's terms. 002 is listed as unrelated with a reason. Verified by inspecting the report against the four pinned requests; no tool run.

observed_facts contain only literal statements from the requests, each citing its id. Inferences are in interpretations and prefixed INFERENCE. Unknowns are listed, and the ownership, scope and blocking-behavior questions are routed to chief_of_staff. Verified by inspection.

remaining_uncertainty: The grouping of syn-req-002 as unrelated is a judgment call; if the user wants one monitoring capability for all four, the consolidated set changes.
The report is based only on the four requests as pinned; I did not check whether any existing code or the three FDE checks exist in the repo.
The sha256 of the input was not recomputed.

questions.question: Should syn-req-002 (schema-contract drift checks) be folded into the shared freshness capability as one data-health capability, or kept as a separate capability? The report currently treats it as unrelated.
Who owns the shared freshness capability and the threshold policy configuration, and which team maintains the owner-team mapping used for the SLA grouping?
Should a stale or unmeasured dataset block the pre-review check, raise an alert, or only show a status on the dashboard?
